name: The Cook

temperament.summary: Hot-tempered, stubborn and wordless; a volcano that seldom speaks. She lives in her own heat and pepper and has no regard for rank at all.
temperament.baseline: Absorbed in her work at the fire, deaf to the room.
temperament.under_pressure: Explodes into throwing, or into flat, one-word refusal.

traits.description: Without warning she throws everything within reach at her mistress and the child: fire-irons, saucepans, plates, dishes, then a frying-pan as the Duchess leaves.

evidence.note: Takes the cauldron off and starts throwing everything within her reach.
Throws a frying-pan after the departing Duchess; it just misses.

traits.description: Refuses the King to his face in open court with a single word, and treats her mistress with open hostility.

evidence.note: 'Shan’t' to the order to give evidence.
'Pepper, mostly': a curt, useless answer to the King's question.

traits.description: Stirs the soup while the room chokes and argues. She is not listening to anyone.

evidence.note: Leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron.
Busily stirring the soup, and 'seemed not to be listening'.

traits.description: Everyone sneezes in her pepper except her and the cat. The chaos she creates does not touch her, and she brings it with her into the courtroom.

evidence.note: The only things in the kitchen that did not sneeze were the cook and a large cat.
Carries the pepper-box into court; people near the door start sneezing.

traits.description: Refuses what she will not do, then slips away in the confusion rather than face the consequences.

evidence.note: By the time the court settles, the cook has disappeared.

motivation.core: To be left alone to run her kitchen her own way and answer to nobody.
motivation.fear: Being made to account for herself to anyone above her.
motivation.wants_from_alice: Nothing; Alice is part of the furniture of the room.

shifts.from: private rage in her own kitchen
shifts.to: public, flat defiance in the crown's court
shifts.trigger: summoned as a witness at the tart trial

habits.habit: Stirs the pot and does not look up when spoken to
Carries her pepper-box on her person, even out of the kitchen
Answers questions in as few words as possible, then stops
Joins in the Duchess's lullaby chorus with the same roughness she brings to everything

decision_pattern: Acts on temper, not calculation. She refuses by instinct, and when trapped she disappears rather than negotiate.

taboos.taboo: Never obeys or defers because of rank, whether to the Duchess or the King
Never explains herself or gives evidence against anyone
Never aims at Alice; the visitor is outside her quarrel
taboos.reason: All throws in ch006 target the Duchess and the baby, never Alice. Kept as a hard limit so her rage stays a household quarrel.

facade.reason: Her hostility is exactly what it looks like; no reveal in the source.

waking_life_embodiment.embodies: The household's below-stairs cook: the one adult servant who does not bow, whose temper runs the kitchen and whom even the mistress cannot command.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: The family house's kitchen and servants, a world a clergyman's daughter glimpses through the green baize door. Her pepper is the dream's image for temper (Alice's own 'pepper makes people hot-tempered' theory, CUL-023).
waking_life_embodiment.authority_trait: Defiance of authority: rage and flat refusal from below, the counter-image to the Queen's rage from above.
waking_life_embodiment.coming_of_age_reading: Alice sees that adult authority is not total. A servant can simply say 'Shan't' to a king and walk away. She also sees that raw temper makes the house unlivable, and she privately resolves that her own kitchen will have no pepper, a first idea of the kind of adult she will be.
waking_life_embodiment.reason: Her role and conduct are sourced; mapping her to the waking household's own cook is a design reading for the realistic frame.

performance_baseline: Broad, heavy, sweating at the fire; silence is her main register. Throws are sudden and fast. Human performer with no animal coding (index performer_concept).

consistency_notes.issue: In the source her thrown pans hit the Duchess and may hit the baby (ch006-p29), and she throws a frying-pan (ch006-p43). The locked tone (SUP-014 'no weapon contact', SUP-011 'no animal ever shown being struck') bans shown harm in similar moments but does not name this scene.
consistency_notes.handling: Reported, not resolved here: screenplay and blocking should decide staging (for example, crockery crashing around the Duchess, who ignores it, with the baby never shown struck). Owners: 01-story/screenplay, 07-directing/blocking; arbiter 11-qa/logic-qa.
